Contemporaneous June reports put maximum monthly usage near $8,000 for Anthropic and $14,000 for OpenAI on $200 plans. These figures do not establish actual compute costs, losses per subscriber or the absence of a viable business model. The proposal applies to the numerical assertion, not that broader economic judgment.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI code generation is not a business model; Anthropic and OpenAI let users burn $8,000–$14,000 a month for a $200 subscription.

statement.excerpt: The ability to generate code in a mindless and expensive way that sometimes works and may or may not make developers an indeterminate level of more-productive is not a business model, a point made more obvious by the fact that Anthropic and OpenAI allow users to burn $8000 to $14,000 a month for $200.
statement.document_title: The More You Buy, The More You Lose

our_interpretation: The numerical assertion is the checkable component. 'Not a business model' supplies no separate profitability threshold or deadline.
The post links to Zitron's earlier discussion of a SemiAnalysis subscription experiment. This establishes an analyst-estimate basis, not audited provider costs.
I read the figures as maximum monthly token usage valued at API list prices: approximately $8,000 for Anthropic and $14,000 for OpenAI.
For the ongoing monthly assertion, June 2026 is the latest completed calendar month before the July 28 post. Individual subscription billing cycles need not follow calendar months.
The figures describe estimated monthly allowances extrapolated from usage limits, not necessarily a full month's observed consumption.
criteria.support_condition: Dated testing and contemporaneous pricing establish that the two $200 subscriptions permitted approximately $8,000 and $14,000 of monthly API-equivalent usage, respectively.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable testing or binding plan limits establish materially smaller maximum monthly API-equivalent allowances for either provider.

evidence.explanation: The report describes SemiAnalysis testing and gives approximately $8,000 for Claude Max and $14,000 for ChatGPT Pro at $200 monthly. It explicitly values the allowances using API prices.

This report gives the same two allowances and explains that they are retail API-equivalent values, not the companies' actual spending. It reports the same experiment as e1, so it is not an independent replication.

The original post describes buying subscription plans and running long coding tasks until weekly limits were exhausted. Its readable text confirms the testing approach but omits the chart needed to verify the exact amounts directly.
